entries.text:
Your message came through as the template text ("PASTE_YOUR_FEEDBACK_HERE"), so I had no feedback to work from. This is the first turn, so I've drawn the first design (version 1) from the approved specification, the architecture and the interface inventory. I didn't change the inventory.

What's drawn:
- One screen per target, "Plant list": web-plant-list (route /, at 360, 720 and 1280 px) and android-plant-list (phone portrait and landscape). There is one flow, "water-a-plant": open the list, spot the Due plants, press Watered, then see the same watering on the other target (R5).
- Every obligation in the inventory is drawn, each with its fixture. Loading; List; Empty ("No plants yet."); and "Can't reach Waterlog." with Try again, which also covers the list's 405 and 500 errors. For each row: in flight (button disabled, "Logging…"), failed ("Couldn't log the watering.", row kept as it was) and watered (new last watering, Due label gone, a "Logged a watering for <name>." line). On Android, INTERNET is granted at install, so there's no prompt; if the network is unavailable, the app shows the unreachable state.
- Due is always the text label "Due" plus a coloured left edge, never colour alone (R3.3).
- 10 mockups: 5 static HTML pages for the web, and 5 labelled Android simulations, each with a portrait and a landscape phone. The inventory's sample data has placeholder names and no due plant, so the List and watered states use two fixtures of mine under mockups/data/. They follow the same shape, with real-looking plants, one never watered, and two due.
- Tokens: light and dark themes. Green accent, water blue, amber for Due, red for errors. The header bar is the same deep green in both themes. All 12 text-on-background pairs reach the AA contrast ratio of 4.5 in both themes; the lowest is 6.0. There are also type, spacing, radius and duration scales. The mockups follow your system's light or dark setting.
- Criteria the engine can check: tokens only, token parity, contrast, layout at each width, visible focus, reduced motion, state markers, and logo parity for both targets. There is also one human test per target for R5. Browser back, the keyboard path, system back, the permission prompt and touch can't be checked yet; they're recorded for a person.
- Logo (step 1 of the held-logo sequence): I propose a water drop with a leaf cut out of it, next to the wordmark "Waterlog", in all five variants. The logo slot is now "proposed" (slot version 2, manifest version 2). Per spec section 8, you hold it at this design approval, and the UI stages build with the placeholder. The favicon and app icon stay as the engine's placeholders.

One thing for the Architect: modules.json's asset_paths name logo variant "default", but the logo slot has no "default" variant. Both clients show the logo on the green header bar, so I've scoped the logo parity checks to the "on_dark" variant. ADR-005 expects exactly this kind of correction, and it needs no code change.

I can't approve my own design; it's yours to review.

entries.speaker: owner
entries.text: The previous placeholder was accidental. The deep-green header, green watering button, amber Due label, and light and dark themes sound like a good starting direction. Keep the favicon and Android app icon as placeholders for now, and leave the proposed logo unapproved for the held-logo sequence. Prioritize readable text, generous spacing, obvious watering status, and comfortable phone controls. I have not inspected the mockups yet and am not approving the design. Please identify which preview pages I should inspect. Also explain whether the default versus on_dark logo variant mismatch still needs an Architect correction; changing the parity check alone must not hide an inconsistent asset binding.

entries.speaker: role
entries.text:
I've drawn design version 2 around your four priorities. Nothing is approved: the design and the proposed logo are both yours to review, and the logo stays "proposed" for the held-logo sequence. The favicon and Android app icon are still the engine's placeholders. I didn't touch the asset files or the manifest, so their digests and versions are unchanged. I didn't change the inventory either.

What changed:
- **Readable text.** Type scale goes up to sm 16 / md 18 / lg 22 / xl 28 (was 14/16/20/24). Nothing in the app is below 16 px. Interval and last watering are body size with their values in bold ("Every **7 days**", "Last watered **9 Oct 2026, 10:30**").
- **Generous spacing.** Spacing scale goes up to 4/8/16/24/32/48 (was 4/8/12/16/24/32). Cards have 16 px between them and 16–24 px of padding.
- **Obvious watering status.**
  - A due plant gets three cues: the "Due" label (bold amber pill with an outline and a drop glyph), an 8 px amber left edge, and an amber-tinted card. It is still never colour alone.
  - The summary line shows the due count in bold ("4 plants · **2 due**").
  - A plant you just watered shows "✓ Watered just now" in a new blue "done" colour, alongside the existing "Logged a watering for <name>." confirmation.
  - A failed watering shows a bold "Couldn't log the watering. Try again." under the row.
- **Comfortable phone controls.** A new touch token sets 48 px/dp as the minimum height for every button. On Android portrait, and on the web at 360 px, Watered is a full-width button under the plant's details. At 720 px and above it sits at the row's right and is at least 160 px wide.
- **Contrast.** I added tokens: due_surface, done_bg/done_text, space.touch and space.edge. Five new text pairs bring the total to 17, and all clear AA in both themes. The lowest is 6.0 (light) and 6.5 (dark), for the disabled button text.
- **Unchanged.** The deep-green header (the same in both themes), the green Watered button, light and dark themes, the screens, states, flow and navigation.

**Preview pages to inspect** (paths under .surety/design/):
1. mockups/web/plant-list-ok.html: due vs not-due rows, text size, spacing. Resize the window to 360, 720 and 1280 px.
2. mockups/web/plant-list-watering.html: watered ("Watered just now"), in flight ("Logging…") and failed rows side by side.
3. mockups/android/plant-list-ok.html: phone portrait and landscape, full-width buttons, the due treatment.
4. mockups/android/plant-list-watering.html: the same three row states on the phone.
5. mockups/web/plant-list-unreachable.html and mockups/android/plant-list-unreachable.html: the error wording and the Try again button.
6. Briefly: the loading and empty pages for each target.

Switch your system to dark mode and reload to see the dark theme. The Android pages are labelled simulations, not the app running.

**The logo variant mismatch: yes, it still needs an Architect correction.** My parity checks don't resolve it. The approved modules.json (and ADR-005) bind slot logo, variant "default", to public/assets/logo.svg and android/assets/logo.png. The logo slot has no "default" variant: its variants are full, compact, monochrome, on_light and on_dark. So the binding names a file the manifest doesn't have.

My criteria compare those paths against on_dark, which is the variant the design really uses: both clients show the logo on the deep-green header in both themes. But that only makes the checks pass against my choice. It leaves the module map pointing at a nonexistent variant, which is exactly the hidden inconsistency you're warning about.

I also won't add a "default" variant to the logo as a copy of on_dark. That would paper over the mismatch the same way.

The correction belongs to the Architect, under ADR-005's own rule that asset_paths is corrected and nothing else changes:
- Change both asset_paths entries from variant "default" to "on_dark".
- State that android/assets/logo.png is a raster derived from the on_dark SVG, and give its size. The variant is SVG, so the Android parity check compares by derivation, not byte for byte.

Until that correction is made, the binding and the parity checks disagree. I recommend you don't treat the logo parity checks as meaningful until then. I raised this last turn; the engine recorded it as a defect but doesn't route it to you, so it needs to go to the Architect directly.

entries.speaker: role
entries.text:
I looked at the saved design and the current inventory. I didn't change the inventory, add any screens, or touch the logo, favicon, app icon or manifest. The logo is still "proposed" and both icons are still placeholders. Nothing is approved.

**What I found.** The saved screens.json already mapped all four obligations, each to the existing Plant list screen on its target with the inventory's own fixture:
- web/page and web/design_tokens: web-plant-list, mockup mockups/web/plant-list-ok.html
- android/api_base_url and android/simulation: android-plant-list, mockup mockups/android/plant-list-ok.html

The engine still reports them uncovered. The one difference from the states it accepts is that each screen's `interfaces` list named only list_plants and log_watering. I couldn't run the design check myself, so I've inferred that this is the cause.

**What I changed (design version 3, screens.json and design.json only):**
- web-plant-list now also lists `page` and `design_tokens`, the files that implement it.
- android-plant-list now also lists `api_base_url` and `simulation`, the config its requests are built on and its labelled preview.
- Each screen's notes say what "ok" means for these files and that they have no data shape.

**The conflict for the Architect.** These four are files of the UI modules, not interfaces the screens draw states of:
- page is the web screen itself.
- design_tokens is its CSS token binding, which the tokens_only and token_parity criteria already check.
- api_base_url is one config constant.
- simulation is the preview of the Android screen.

The inventory lists all four as shape_known false, but it still derives an "ok" state obligation for each. The check reference says a screen that uses an interface of unknown shape is refused with DESIGN_INTERFACE_SHAPE_UNKNOWN. If the next save swaps DESIGN_STATE_UNCOVERED for that error, these obligations can't be covered honestly as the inventory classifies them.

The fix belongs to the Architect. Either record these as module paths or implementation files instead of interfaces, or give each one a shape and a state that means something to a user. I've raised one contract_conflict per interface so this reaches you. While they're open, the design can't be approved (DESIGN_INTERFACE_DISPUTED) until you settle them.

**Still open from before:** modules.json binds logo variant "default", which the logo slot doesn't have. That still needs the Architect's asset_paths correction to "on_dark".

Please save, and tell me what the check reports.
